The proper functioning of this protein complex is critical for developmental processes, including left/right patterning and potentially other cilia-dependent signaling pathways.

The cellular consequence of Polycystin-1-like protein 1 activity is the regulation of cilium calcium concentration, which in turn affects various signaling pathways. At the tissue level, this regulation is crucial for the proper specification of left/right asymmetry and potentially other developmental processes that rely on ciliary function.

The systemic significance of Polycystin-1-like protein 1 function is evident in its association with congenital malformations and diseases, such as biliary atresia and congenital chylothorax, as seen in Pkd1l1-deficient mice and humans with PKD1L1 mutations. Under venous shear stress (1-6 dyn/cm2), Nitric oxide synthase is activated, leading to an increase in nitric oxide (NO) production.
